summary: Big House Mountain, the western peak of House Mountain, is listed only as an unconfirmed site; no lookout tower is described there.

facts.status_note: Listed only as an unconfirmed site; no lookout tower is confirmed here.

access.note: A trail from near the shelter in the saddle reaches the top of Big House Mountain.

visit.trail_note: A two-mile trail to the saddle starts where the state road ends; a trail from the shelter leads to the top.

land.funding: Rockbridge Conservation raised $150,000 in the late 1980s, donated to the Virginia Outdoors Foundation, which with another $175,000 bought and permanently protected the land

evidence.supports: the site is listed only as unconfirmed, on the Virginia list
Big House Mountain, Rockbridge, Unconfirmed type, Unknown status
evidence.quote: Big House Mountain Rockbridge 37.83101 -79.56195 Unconfirmed Unknown

evidence.supports: House Mountain is a Rockbridge County landmark, 5 miles west of Lexington
evidence.quote: House Mountain is a dominant Rockbridge County landmark. It is located 5 miles west of Lexington.

evidence.supports: House Mountain is made of two peaks, Big House and Little House
evidence.quote: Though it is referred to as a singular mountain, House Mountain is comprised of two mountains: Big House and Little House.

evidence.supports: Big House is the western peak at 3,645 feet; Little House is the eastern peak at 3,386 feet, lower
evidence.quote: the saddle sits at the base of the cliffs of Big House Mountain (3,645 feet) to the west and the laurel thickets of Little House Mountain (3,386 feet) to the east.

evidence.supports: the saddle was once pasture and apple orchard; homesteads stood on the mountain and in the saddle
evidence.quote: Once a pasture and apple orchard, the saddle sits at the base of the cliffs of Big House Mountain

evidence.supports: homesteads once stood high on the mountain and in the saddle
evidence.quote: A number of homesteads once stood high on the mountain and in the saddle.

evidence.supports: late 1980s fundraising toward buying the top of the mountain
evidence.quote: raising $150,000 to put toward the purchase of the top of the mountain

evidence.supports: Virginia Outdoors Foundation bought and protected the land as a Reserve
evidence.quote: which with an additional $175,000 was able to purchase and permanently protect the land as a Reserve

evidence.supports: the House Mountain Reserve covers 968 acres
evidence.quote: There are 968 acres of protected land in the House Mountain Reserve.
There is a camping shelter, camping sites, and spring in the saddle.

evidence.supports: a trail from near the shelter gives access to the top of Big House Mountain
evidence.quote: Visitors may access the top of Big House Mountain via a trail that begins near the shelter.

evidence.supports: the two-mile trail to the saddle starts at the end of the state road
evidence.quote: The two-mile trail to the saddle is a mountain road heading west from the end of the state road.

notes_for_editor: No source read describes a fire lookout on Big House Mountain. The Forest Fire Lookout Association's Virginia list has it under Unconfirmed Sites, with type Unconfirmed and status Unknown. The Rockbridge Conservation page is the only substantive source and describes the reserve and trail, not a tower. Two web searches found nothing more. Consider marking the record unconfirmed or hidden, since the site may never have had a lookout.
